newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks stroll to narrowly mixed end.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks stroll to narrowly mixed end.

text.p: A slow Australian share market ended barely changed on Thursday as the market drifted with little motivation or interest from traders.
The All Ordinaries index lost 1.8 points to 2,452.6.
The market dipped sharply early after the Dow fell, quickly pruned those losses and by lunch had found its niche in a narrow four point trading band just below square.
"I suppose the bias was down but there wasn't much in it," said a dealer at a Sydney brokerage.
"The banks were down early although National Australia Bank was the odd one out. It was probably overdone yesterday."
National Australia Bank recouped nearly all of its Wednesday losses, adding 20 cents to A$16.05 (US$12.68). The other big banks ended much as the rest of the market, narrowly mixed.
Labour force data failed to have any serious impact.
"Unemployment was a little worse than the market expected and that helped the bonds but didn't do much for us really," said a Melbourne broker.

Results continued, with Australia's largest retailer Coles Myer gaining 13 cents to an intraday high of A$6.04 before easing to close just two cents higher at A$5.93 after its sharply higher first half net profit of A$273.6 million and forecasts of similar second half profit growth.

Pay TV operator Australis Media topped turnover lists with brokers saying speculation of rationalisation in the profit-scarce industry was sparking investor's interest. Its shares closed three cents higher at 18.5 cents on heavy turnover of 22.98 million shares.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about seven to five, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
